defect_class: A screenshot capture written by an implementer is not taken in the state it names: interactions that produce the state run after the screenshot, or the pointer is left on the last clicked control so hover ink enters the baseline.
why_picked: 1. Defect class: a capture test records a state other than the one it names — the state's interactions run after its screenshot, or transient pointer state is left on the page. 2. No rule covers it for implementers: the capture rules ('A capture reached through a click also asserts the state it clicked into, and parks the pointer before it is taken', visual-verify-verifier.md:49) reach only the verifier; the implementer instructions for capture tasks say only how to get a stack (the quoted One stack for the verification tasks paragraph), and a grep of implement.md, sdd-dispatch.md and engineering-principles.md for pointer, mouse.move, hover ink and park finds nothing. 3. It generalises: two separate implementer dispatches in this run hit it — Task 4 (0470e14b) picked Projects and Task size after its last screenshot, costing visual round 2; Task 5 (bde84fe0) left the pointer on Big, costing round 3 — and every planned capture task and in-run visual fix task is written by an implementer, not the verifier. 4. It is not patch accretion: one set of capture rules for whoever writes a capture, a pointer to the verifier's existing rules rather than a copy.
before:
**Before the first task whose `**Files:**` only add end-to-end specs, fidelity captures or their
baselines goes out** — dispatched under `sdd`, or started by the parent on an `inline` run — the
parent starts the canonical worktree's stack once, by the start rule of **Resolve the run
instructions** (`skills/flow/verify-and-handoff.md`) — its failure, refused-start and
protected-service handling included — then runs any build the plan's Global Constraints name
for those tasks, then `check-dev-stack-fresh.sh <canonical-worktree>`: exit 1 is a failed start,
and exit 2 puts `Freshness: unverified — <the guard's reason>` in every such task's prompt.
Every such task, and every wave copy it runs in, runs against that stack's worktree-resolved
URLs, which its prompt names, and starts, stops and rebuilds nothing. The stack stays up for
`flow.verify`.
